title.en: A Picture Record of a Royal Birthday

summaryEn: Uigwe were detailed reports, full of pictures, of royal ceremonies and projects. Hoya opens the Wonhaeng Eulmyo Jeongni Uigwe, the record of King Jeongjo's 1795 celebration for his mother's 60th birthday.
hoyaIntroEn: Let's open a royal report full of pictures, made for a big birthday celebration!
hoyaOutroEn: Words and pictures kept the royal celebration alive. Now you know what an uigwe is!
learningGoalsEn: Know that an 의궤 (uigwe) recorded a royal ceremony or project in words and pictures so later generations could follow it.
Know that uigwe list the people who took part, including craftspeople.
Know that a 반차도 (banchado) is a long picture of a procession, usually drawn as if seen from above.
Know that the 1795 feast for Lady Hyegyeong at Bongsudang is recorded in the Annals and in the Wonhaeng Eulmyo Jeongni Uigwe, which was printed with metal type.
Read and recognize 잔치 (janchi), 그림 (geurim), 어머니 (eomeoni), 환갑 (hwangap) and 장인 (jangin).

origin.noteEn: Heritage history, researched from the sources listed on the Sources screen.

keywords.en: illustrated record of a royal event
the uigwe of King Jeongjo's 1795 royal trip

scenes.narrationEn: When the Joseon court held a big event, such as a royal wedding, a banquet or the rebuilding of a palace, officials made an {kw:uigwe}: a detailed report in words and pictures.
scenes.captionEn: A royal event report in words and pictures

keyword.en: illustrated record of a royal event

scenes.artBrief: An open old book with a colorful painted page of a ceremony beside a page of neat brush writing (no readable text); Hoya leaning in to look.

art.altEn: Hoya leans in to look at an open uigwe: a painted picture of a royal event beside pages of neat brush writing.

scenes.narrationEn: Why? So that next time, people could hold the same kind of event properly. Each uigwe recorded the steps, the people, the costs and the materials, like a final report.
scenes.captionEn: A guide for holding similar events
scenes.artBrief: Officials checking items off against an open uigwe: bolts of cloth, bowls, flags and lanterns laid out in a courtyard.

art.altEn: An official checks cloth, bowls, a flag and a lantern laid out in a courtyard against the written record.

scenes.narrationEn: Uigwe even listed the people who took part, from high officials to skilled craftspeople. Their names and roles were written down, too.
scenes.artBrief: A carpenter, a painter and an embroiderer at work in a palace workshop, each proud of their craft.

art.altEn: In a palace workshop a carpenter, a painter and an embroiderer each work carefully at their own craft.

scenes.narrationEn: In 1795, King Jeongjo traveled with his mother, Lady Hyegyeong, to the new city of Hwaseong in Suwon for a grand celebration of her 60th birthday.
scenes.artBrief: A long, colorful royal procession winding along a road toward a fortress city; two ornate palanquins at the center.

art.altEn: A long royal procession with a red palanquin between two horses travels toward the walled city of Hwaseong.

scenes.narrationEn: In 1795, the old lunar calendar had an extra month after the second month. On day 13 of that month, the king held a grand feast for his mother at Bongsudang Hall in Hwaseong. The Annals record that day.
scenes.captionEn: A grand feast at Bongsudang Hall
scenes.artBrief: A festive palace hall with tables of food, musicians and dancers in bright costumes, and an honored elderly lady seated under a canopy.

art.altEn: Court dancers perform beside a feast table, and a fine curtain screens the seat of Lady Hyegyeong, the guest of honour.

scenes.narrationEn: The king also gave gifts of silk to elderly people who took part in the celebration.
scenes.artBrief: Smiling elderly men in plain traditional clothes receiving folded bolts of silk in a sunny courtyard.

art.altEn: Elderly guests of the 1795 celebration each receive a folded bolt of silk, a gift from the king.

scenes.narrationEn: The record of this trip, the {kw:wonhaeng-eulmyo-jeongni-uigwe}, is full of pictures. Some are {kw:banchado}: long pictures of a royal procession, usually drawn as if seen from high above, showing where everyone walked or stood.
scenes.captionEn: Long pictures of the royal procession
scenes.artBrief: A bird's-eye view of a long procession: rows of tiny figures, horses, flags and palanquins arranged neatly along a path.

art.altEn: Hoya studies printed procession pages, drawn as if from high above, with rows of tiny figures, horses and a palanquin.

scenes.narrationEn: Unusually, this uigwe was printed with metal movable type, so more copies could be shared. Its pictures are prints, too. In 2007, UNESCO added the Joseon uigwe to the Memory of the World.
scenes.artBrief: Small metal type pieces in a tray next to a freshly printed picture page and the printing tools beside it.

art.altEn: A frame of small metal type sits beside a freshly printed picture page: this uigwe was printed with metal type.

facts.claimEn: Uigwe record, in text and illustrations, major royal ceremonies and state projects such as royal weddings, banquets, funerals, receptions of envoys and the rebuilding of palaces.
facts.claimKo: 의궤는 왕실의 혼인, 잔치, 장례, 사신 접대, 궁궐 중건 같은 국가 의례와 행사를 글과 그림으로 기록한 것이다.

facts.claimEn: In 1795, King Jeongjo went to the new city of Hwaseong with his mother, Lady Hyegyeong, for the celebration of her 60th birthday (hoegap).
facts.claimKo: 1795년 정조는 어머니 혜경궁 홍씨의 회갑을 기념하여 어머니를 모시고 새 도시 화성에 행차하였다.

sources.title: 원행을묘정리의궤(園幸乙卯整理儀軌)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 『원행을묘정리의궤』는 1797년 정리소에서 혜경궁 홍씨의 회갑연 행사를 날짜별로 정리해 간행한 의궤이다. 1795년 윤2월 9일 정조가 회갑을 맞은 혜경궁 홍씨를 모시고 현륭원과 화성 행궁에 행차하여 올린 진연 및 환궁 후의 행사 등을 정리소에서 날짜별로 기록한 책이다.

sources.title: 봉수당진찬도(奉壽堂進饌圖)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 1795년 윤2월 13일 화성행궁의 봉수당에서 거행된 혜경궁 홍씨의 회갑연을 그린 조선시대 기록화.

sources.title: Hwaseong Fortress (World Heritage)
sources.quoteOrLocator: "In February 1795, when the construction was in its final phase, the king visited Hwaseong with his mother Lady Hyegyeong to hold a banquet to celebrate her 60th birthday. The new city was selected as the venue for the grand event"

facts.claimEn: The banquet for Lady Hyegyeong was held at Bongsudang in the Hwaseong temporary palace on the 13th day of the leap 2nd lunar month (yun-2-wol, the extra month inserted after the 2nd month) of 1795, as recorded in the Annals of King Jeongjo.
facts.claimKo: 혜경궁을 위한 진찬은 1795년(정조 19) 윤2월 13일 화성행궁의 봉수당에서 열렸으며, 정조실록에 기록되어 있다.

sources.title: 정조실록 42권, 정조 19년 윤2월 13일 을미 1번째기사 「봉수당에 나아가 혜경궁을 위해 연회를 베풀다」
sources.publisher: 국사편찬위원회 조선왕조실록 DB (National Institute of Korean History)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 정조실록 42권, 정조 19년 윤2월 13일 을미 1/4 기사 (1795년): "봉수당(奉壽堂)에 나아가 혜경궁을 위해 연회를 베풀었다." 原文: "御奉壽堂, 進饌于惠慶宮。"

sources.title: 봉수당진찬도(奉壽堂進饌圖)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 진찬은 정조 일행이 화성에 도착한지 3일째 되는 윤2월 13일에 화성행궁의 내당인 봉수당에서 거행되었다.

facts.claimEn: On that day the king ordered gifts of silk for elderly people who had taken part in the banquet.
facts.claimKo: 같은 날 정조는 연회에 참여한 노인들에게 비단을 내리도록 명하였다.

sources.title: 정조실록 42권, 정조 19년 윤2월 13일 을미 3번째기사 「연회의 반열에 참여한 노인들에게 비단 등을 주고 수원부 성 내외에 급복을 명하다」
sources.publisher: 국사편찬위원회 조선왕조실록 DB (National Institute of Korean History)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 정조실록 42권, 정조 19년 윤2월 13일 을미 3/4 기사: "연회를 베풀 때 반열에 참여한 노인으로서 70세 이상이 되는 자 및 61세가 되는 사람들에게 각각 비단 1필(匹)씩을 하사하는 동시에" 原文: "命進饌時參班老人, 七十以上及六十一歲人, 各賜帛一匹"

facts.claimEn: Banchado are pictures of court ceremonies and processions that show the placement of participants, generally drawn from a high, bird's-eye viewpoint; the Wonhaeng Eulmyo Jeongni Uigwe includes 63 pages of banchado among 112 illustrated pages.
facts.claimKo: 반차도는 궁중 행사와 행렬에서 참여자의 배치를 보여 주는 그림으로, 대개 높은 곳에서 내려다보는 부감법으로 그렸으며, 『원행을묘정리의궤』에는 반차도 63면을 포함해 도식 112면이 실려 있다.

sources.title: 반차도 (국가유산이야기 > 의궤정보)
sources.publisher: 국가유산청 국가유산포털 (Korea Heritage Service, National Heritage Portal)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 궁중 행사의 의식과 늘어선 관원들의 배치 상황이 정확히 묘사되어 있어 ... 높은 위치에서 내려다보는 식의 부감법(俯瞰法)을 사용하여 그리는 것이 일반적이다.

sources.title: 원행을묘정리의궤(園幸乙卯整理儀軌)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 「화성행행도(華城行幸圖)」를 비롯하여 「봉수당진찬도(奉壽堂進饌圖)」 ... 등 도식 49면, 반차도 63면으로 총 112면이 판화로 제작되어 실려 있다.

sources.title: Memory of the World Register – Uigwe: The Royal Protocols of the Joseon Dynasty, Ref N° 2006-48 (nomination form, PDF)
sources.quoteOrLocator: §1 Summary: "In particular, the pictorial materials, such as “Banchado” and “Doseol” illustrate the rituals and ceremonies of the time with a sophistication and vividness that matches the visual materials of the present day."

facts.claimEn: The Wonhaeng Eulmyo Jeongni Uigwe was printed with metal movable type (Jeongnija); this was unusual because most uigwe were handwritten, and printed uigwe circulated more widely. Its 112 pages of pictures, including the banchado, were made as prints (panhwa).
facts.claimKo: 『원행을묘정리의궤』는 금속활자(정리자)로 간행되었는데, 의궤 대부분이 필사본이었던 데 비해 드문 경우이며 활자본은 더 널리 배포되었다. 그림 112면은 판화로 제작되었다.

sources.title: 원행을묘정리의궤(園幸乙卯整理儀軌)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 최초의 활자본 의궤로 금속활자로 간행되었다. ... 총 112면이 판화로 제작되어 실려 있다.

verification.notes: Third independent pass. All Sillok entries (Taejong 4/2/8 #4; Jeongjo 19/leap2/13 #1 and #3) re-fetched from sillok.history.go.kr and compared to original Chinese/Korean text. Every non-UNESCO URL cited was re-fetched fresh and every quote segment machine-matched, plus heritage.go.kr 국가유산 설명 text loaded from the portal's own ajax file (DATA1/heritage/hub_img/html/cul_*.html). UNESCO register pages for all four items verified via Internet Archive (registration years 1997/2001/2007/2011 with exact wording); Uigwe nomination PDF re-extracted and quotes/section numbers verified; Seungjeongwon nomination PDF could not be re-fetched (captcha) so the author's saved text was used, with other sources backing each fact. Corrections this pass: poswae schedule mistranslation (격 2년 = every third year, not every other year), 'dried herbs' removed, ep5 f4 quote exactified, 3 vocab words not appearing in scenes removed, ep5 f8 second source (정병모 판화사적 연구) and ep6 f3 festival official site added, UNESCO locators replaced by exact page wording, ep3 f7 3,045+198 clarification.

authorNotes: Narration omits the ages in the silk-gift entry (70+ and those turning 61) because they come from a single source; the Korean line '어르신' is a vocabulary item. 회갑 (source term) and 환갑 (everyday term) both mean the 60th birthday; 환갑 is taught. The feast date is given on the lunar calendar as recorded; the KHS English page says 'February 1795', which refers to the lunar leap 2nd month. The leap-month wording was rewritten simply ('an extra leap month after the second month'). The Hwaseong feast (13th of the leap 2nd month) took place during the 1795 trip celebrating her 60th year; her actual birthday fell in the 6th lunar month and the Encyclopedia notes a formal feast on 6/18 in Seoul, so narration says 'a celebration of her 60th birthday' and never says the Hwaseong feast was on the birthday itself. Revision: the uigwe is now named (원행을묘정리의궤); banchado described as 'long pictures' not paintings; 'woodblock' was REMOVED - Korean authorities (Encyclopedia of Korean Culture) say only 판화 (prints), and no Korean institutional source found says woodblock specifically (a Cambridge/Amsterdam UP page suggested by a checker did not mention woodcuts when re-fetched). The encyclopedia calls this 'the first uigwe printed with movable type'; narration says 'unusually' to stay conservative. UNESCO page text is paraphrased (unesco.org unreachable for re-quoting); UNESCO nomination-form quotes were re-checked against a saved copy of the PDF; the draft's banchado caption quote ('Banchado in color ... excellent clarity') could not be found in the PDF text and was replaced by the §1 Summary sentence on Banchado and Doseol. Omitted: the length of a painting (15.4 m, single source), page counts beyond f7, the story of Prince Sado (tragic), and the 1866 removal of Oegyujanggak uigwe to France and their 2011 return (war-related). PASS 3: second source for 판화 found (정병모, 판화사적 연구: 'prints' - and specifically 목판화, woodblock prints, with 정리자 metal type); narration stays at the more general 'prints'. Silk gifts (f6) confirmed directly in the original Annals entry text (命進饌時參班老人, 七十以上及六十一歲人, 各賜帛一匹); single primary source kept, no numbers in narration.
